title: Design System: jiuaxl. — The Knowledge Panel

motion.name: ease-out-quart
motion.purpose: Default easing for all UI motion: route transitions, underline slide, dropdown reveals, hover tints. No bounce/elastic anywhere in this system.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Micro-interactions: hover tints, focus rings, accordion caret rotation.

motion.name: duration-base
motion.purpose: Route transitions, nav underline slide, suggestion dropdown reveal.

motion.name: duration-stagger-step
motion.purpose: Per-item delay for result-row and menu-grid stagger, capped at ~10 items / 500ms total.

motion.name: duration-hero
motion.purpose: Cap for the Landing view's single choreographed hero entrance.

narrative.overview: The premise: Jiu Axl is notable enough that searching his name surfaces the real Google apparatus, a search bar, a results list, People Also Ask, a People Also Search For rail, a Knowledge Panel, right down to a did you mean 404. The whole site is that Knowledge Panel, expanded outward into a full portfolio. It's a playful, obviously-a-wink pastiche rather than a deadpan forgery: the fun is in how convincingly well-crafted the joke is, not in fooling anyone into thinking it's really google.com. Precision and craft carry the personality; the page never winks with a caption explaining the joke, it just executes the bit extremely well.
keyCharacteristics: Google's own documented Material grey scale and text colors, used verbatim
One typeface family (Satoshi) doing all the work through weight and scale contrast
SERP furniture is real navigational structure, not decoration
Motion mimics real Google micro-interactions, not generic marketing-site flourish

rules.name: The Flat Palette Rule
rules.body: Every neutral is a real, documented Google Material grey. When in doubt about a new grey, don't invent one; borrow from Google's own published scale.

rules.name: The Truncation Rule
rules.body: Result descriptions cap at 80 characters plus an ellipsis; this is the de facto line-length control in place of a prose measure.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Never add box-shadow for decorative depth. If a surface needs to read as raised, use a tonal fill (Grey 50/100) or a 1px Grey 300 border instead.

dos: Do use Google's real documented greys for all neutral UI, not invented hex values.
Do keep every surface flat; depth comes from tonal fills or a 1px Grey 300 border, never a shadow.
Do let SERP furniture carry real content and navigation, not decoration.
Do treat motion as a Google-authenticity anchor.
Do provide a prefers-reduced-motion fallback for every animation added.
donts: Don't use glassy SaaS cards, gradient hero sections, or glassmorphism-by-default.
Don't build identical icon-card grids, tiny uppercase tracked eyebrows, or 01/02/03 numbered section scaffolding.
Don't add a card-hover-lift shadow to result rows.
Don't use border-left/border-right as a colored accent stripe.
Don't source or forge Google Sans/Product Sans to chase authenticity.
Don't apply the same scroll-fade-in to whole section wrappers; stagger belongs to individual result rows.
